name: Functional, divisional and matrix structures
purpose: Which grouping logic does the organisation chart show?
apply: Link chart and configuration: functional ↔ machine bureaucracy, divisional ↔ divisional form, matrix ↔ adhocracy
pitfalls: The chart shows only grouping, not coordination or power

name: Mintzberg's 5 coordination mechanisms

parts.label: Standardisation of work processes
points: Rules and routines fix the how

parts.label: Standardisation of skills
points: Training fixes what to expect of each other

apply: What is fixed in advance? The boss → the how → the what → the training → nothing
pitfalls: All are used; name the dominant one and justify with case facts
example: Bar → processes · traders +15 % → outputs · basketball → mutual adjustment · Roman wars → direct supervision.

name: Mintzberg's 5 parts of the organisation
purpose: Who does what in the organisation?

parts.label: Support staff
points: Services outside the work flow: legal, cleaning

apply: Map the case's actors onto the five parts and say which part is strongest
example: CEO · director of production · machine operators · planning/training · cleaning.

name: Mintzberg's 5 configurations
purpose: Which structural configuration characterises the organisation – and does it fit?
apply: 1 Key parts → 2 coordination → 3 pull → 4 contingency factors → 5 configuration → 6 fit and recommendation
Real organisations are often hybrids (e.g. professional bureaucracy with adhocratic features)
pitfalls: Divisional form: key part is the middle line, not the apex
Adhocracy still coordinates – by costly mutual adjustment
example: OpenAI mock: professional bureaucracy + adhocracy with elements of simple structure.
